facts.P1_fx_receipts: Yes, through Ethiopian banks; service exporters keep 100% in a retention account.
facts.P2_fcy_account: Yes, for qualifying income; FX savings accounts no longer need a USD 100 minimum.
facts.P3_local_gateways: Chapa is a licensed gateway; whether individuals can sign up is unconfirmed.
facts.L1_registration: Formal route: trade registration and a business licence via eTrade, plus a TIN.
facts.L2_tax_id: TIN from the Ministry of Revenues, linked to your Fayda digital ID.
facts.L3_income_tax_foreign: Worldwide income taxed at 0–35%; small sellers may pay 2–9% on sales.
facts.L4_vat_gst: 15% VAT above ETB 2 million a year; qualifying exports are zero-rated.
facts.L5_data_protection: Register with the Ethiopian Communications Authority before processing personal data.
facts.L6_consumer_ecommerce: Buyers can return within 7 days for a full refund.
facts.L7_incentives: Keep 100% of service-export earnings in foreign currency since February 2026.

watch_out.text: Without a TIN and licence, payers withhold 30% instead of 3%.
Banks may ask for a TIN and business licence for a retention account.
PayPal accounts in Ethiopia can only send and shop, not receive.
